learning: Iteration 5 showed that narrowing the track improved the oval and s-bend, but oscillation rose above 0.25. Read the next race against iteration 5 (112.54) on each track. If oval oscillation stays below 0.25 and s-bend max_error falls, kp/track is the right control. If oscillation is still high, lower kp further before changing geometry again.
notes: Complete robot for the Builder's wheel_track 0.09 m geometry. kp is lowered from 4.0 to 3.5 so that kp / wheel_track (38.9) stays close to iteration 5's 40.0, offsetting the higher effective yaw gain.
rationale: Iteration 5 (wheel_track 0.10 m, kp 4.0) is the best result at 112.54. Its oval steering_oscillation rose to 0.277, above the 0.25 caution level. Under the contract's yaw relation, effective yaw gain scales with kp / wheel_track. Iteration 0 gave 4/0.12 = 33.3, iteration 5 gave 4/0.10 = 40.0, and the Builder's 0.09 m track with kp 4.0 would give 44.4, about 11 percent more than iteration 5 and 33 percent more than the baseline. To avoid compounding oscillation, I lower kp to 3.5, which gives 38.9, slightly below iteration 5's gain. This keeps the test close to the best-known steering response while the Builder's geometry change (wheel_track 0.09 m, all else fixed) is measured. ki, kd, base_speed, sensor weights and line_loss match iteration 5. Expected: s-bend max_error near 0.061 to 0.062 m, oval oscillation near or below 0.25, and a score in the 113 to 120 range. Risk: lower kp may slow correction on the s-bend, so line loss could stay at 2 per run. If the score falls below 112.54, the Builder's revert to 0.10 m applies.
